## About Me

I am a current PhD student in the [Department of Population Health and Quantitative Studies](https://case.edu/medicine/pqhs/) at Case Western Reserve University. My research interests broadly span biostatistical methods, nutritional epidemiology, food system sustainability, cardiovascular health, and graph learning. 

## Education & Background

In 2026, I graduated from The College of William and Mary with a Bachelor's of Science in Data Science and a minor in Public Health. Here, I developed a background in both theoretical and applied statistics, computational tools, and public health foundations. 

I have worked for the [William & Mary Global Research Institute](https://www.wm.edu/offices/global-research/) as a research assistant under the direction of [Dr. Zach Conrad](https://www.zachsconrad.com/). As a proud member of the Nutritional Epidemiology and Food Systems Analytics (NEFSA) lab, I gained valuable experience researching food waste and the sustainability impacts of various diets. Here, I honed my research chops and developed a passion for food systems research that I carry with me to this day!
